My approach is simple: Prep for your day.

Literally, just start there. Develop an EDC that you can and will use. That's the shit you're going to carry on you at all times. Maybe build a small go bag with the essentials. Stuff you'll use everyday, A few things you might need in an emergency and stuff you'll definitely need in an emergency. Whatever you do, make sure it's all readily usable. Keep it kinda low on the tech end.

After that, you can go ahead and build a bug out bag if you like but try to keep it real and useful. Make sure you have a location to which you can go and build the bag with practicality in mind. It should be something you're going to grab, toss in your car and head to the location directly to wait out the shit. You'll be coming back so only enough supplies to take with you for three days if you need to break into it.

The next step is the INCH bag if you don't have that bunker to ride out anything. With this one, home and all else is going to ride on your back. It's going to be heavy as balls and you're going to be doing a lotta hunting, foraging, fishing and basically, home is wherever you're going to be able to set up camp for a night or two. It's going to be more tool heavy than anything.

The trick is, break that shit down into bite-sized chunks. Prep for your day FIRST and foremost. If you don't, the rest of these zombie/doomsday/hurricane/natural disaster preps won't mean a fucking thing. You need a solid foundation first and you need to stick with it.

For beginners in the US, I'd suggest Sparrows or Peterson (government steel, not carbon steel with plastic handles, not rubber). The handles make it a lot easier to practice since they spread the force out against yout finger a little more. Yes, you lose a little feedback, but pain dissuades practice.

Your right, especially when it comes to beginners. I advanced pretty quickly but I felt the pain your talking about. I needed my lockpicking fix and the Praxis kit is not very friendly to your fingers when your spending all day on that one lock you've just gotta pick.

There are a few things you can do though. My preferred way is heat shrink tubing, (see bottom for textured grips) there is also the marine grade type thats a little thicker and has heat activated glue but all can be cut to size and slipped over the handle then quickly shrunk to a tight fit with a small butane torch.

Lately I've been having a go at making my own picks and by extension handles. The Praxis kit picks have plenty of holes pre-cut for grip, but it also makes them ideal for epoxy to get between them, so you use wooden lollypop sticks, which you can sand then stain. Although right now I'm starting to use plastic cut to size from some coloured chopping boards bought at the £1 shop.

Also for even more budget in "comfort on a budget" (the price of electrical tape and scissors) this works well, but after time you might want to cut off and renew as the tape slips as it gets warm with repeated use. First cut a strip of electrical tape long ways, re-wrapping it around a pen can help with directing it to the shape you want when unwinding on your pick later. You want thin strips wrapped around the same area creating a raised band. Two of these spaced a fingers width apart and then wrapped over with full width electric tape create a very ergonomic and most importantly customised grip. More intricate and even more ergonomic designs just requires more of the same, except instead of strips/bands wrapped and stacked around I used little squares stacked on top of each other, then as before wrapping it with whole electrical tape tightly or Heat shrink.
